sep 28 – been seeing posts about 24h stroke treatment window. got curious. checked out the DAWN trial.
sep 29 – DAWN published NEJM 2018. randomized 206 pts, anterior circulation LVO, last known well 6-24h. strict imaging: CT perfusion or DWI, core <21 mL. only ~27% of screened patients actually randomized — eligibility narrow.

sep 30 – also DEFUSE 3 trial: 16h window, similar inclusion (mismatch, core <70 mL). also positive.
– each hour delay after onset reduces odds of good outcome by ~11% relative. so earlier still better even within the window.
oct 1 – AHA/ASA updated guidelines 2018: Class I, Level A for thrombectomy up to 24h in select patients.
– potential harms: vessel perforation ~2–3%, access site hematoma, contrast nephropathy. not trivial.
– cost: thrombectomy can run $20k–50k per case; not all insurance fully covers.
oct 2 – looked up hospital capability: only ~40% of US hospitals have endovascular thrombectomy capability. rural areas especially lack.
– still, stories of patients waking up with stroke, getting thrombectomy, walking out within days are incredible.
oct 3 – news release I saw only used relative risk numbers, no absolute numbers. but the effect size is real.
– unrelated: my uncle had a stroke 5 years ago, didn’t get treatment in time, now has permanent aphasia. makes me think about this.
oct 4 – extra: DAWN trial sponsored by Stryker Neurovascular. lead author Dr. Raul Nogueira.
– also, stroke is the 5th leading cause of death in US (2016 data).
– quick note: the procedure is mechanical thrombectomy—retrievable stent or aspiration. cool tech.
– oh and the NNT of 2.8 means you only need to treat ~3 patients to get one more independent outcome. insane.
